problem:
The equation of a curve is ${x}^{2}+2y=20.$ The tangent line at the point $(2,8)$ intersects the $x$-axis at the point $P.$ What are the coordinates of $P?$

The coordinates of $P$ are $($
{{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$).$
worked_solution:
First of all, we need to find the slope of the tangent line at the point $(2,8).$ 

To find the slope of the tangent line, we will calculate the derivative using implicit differentiation, assuming that $y=y(x).$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+2y & =20 \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}+2y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(20) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(20) \\ 2x+2\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =0 \\ 2\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-2x \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-x.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the slope of the tangent at the point $(2,8)$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(2,\,8)} \\  & ={(-x)|}_{(2,\,8)} \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

We can write the equation of the tangent line at the point $(2,8)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-8 & =-2(x-2) \\ y-8 & =-2x+4 \\ y & =-2x+12\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we just need to find where this tangent line intersects the $x$-axis. At the point $P$ the $y$-coordinate is $0,$ so we set $y=0$ and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}0 & =-2x+12 \\ 2x & =12 \\ x & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of $P$ are $(6,\,0).$
